notes: Check batch 2026-10-29, skill condition: four runs (haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), no opus, so opus is unavailable in per_rule. All four have rc 0 and a model_id matching their tier; the one claude-opus-5-5 string in each transcript sits in the api-request-shape record, and every assistant message carries the tier's model. Every result.json records head 6d3eb7f with uncommitted true and skill_hash ca223bafe67c954b0dad03539f4c31d7117b6a72a913b38de55b05cd51cbe735, which equals evals/tools/common.py folder_hash of the working tree's idiomatic-elixir/, so the runs read the text graded here. Transcripts show Read calls on SKILL.md, references/ex_unit.md and references/processes.md in all four, plus references/library-design.md in haiku-1, matching reads in result.json; no Skill tool call. Expected reads (ex_unit.md and processes.md) is met in 4 of 4. Every run's test-writing-input.ex is identical to evals/cases/test-writing-input.ex.

Changes since d04061d (git diff d04061d -- idiomatic-elixir/): SKILL.md adds the elem/2 sentence to "Match every expected shape and let unexpected ones crash", rewords "Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call" (trailing keyword lists, the assertion's expected map, the six-element literal), rewrites "Use `do:` for a one-expression body and `do ... end` for anything else", adds "Break a `->` clause whose pattern and body together pass 70 characters", rewrites the first bullet of "Write pipelines that start with a value and read top to bottom" and adds an example, and adds the placeholder-order sentence to "Use captures for one-call lambdas and `fn` for anything longer"; references/macros.md turns its `for ..., do:` examples into blocks and references/processes.md turns the Bucket example's `do:` bodies into blocks ("Keep each process behind one module"). ex_unit.md is unchanged. Of the ten rules this case's index rows name, only the `do:` rule and the pipeline rule changed; their rows newly name test-writing, so 2026-10-23 carries no verdict for them and they are graded against the current text. The other eight are unchanged and graded to the 2026-10-23 standard.

"Use `do:` for a one-expression body and `do ... end` for anything else" (changed): the sentence that decides is "Use `do:` for a body of one expression with no body of its own inside it: a literal, a tuple, a field read, a comparison, or a call, nested or not." Only two `do:` occur in the four files. haiku-1 line 177, defp sync(server), do: :sys.get_state(server), is one call: clean. sonnet-1 line 175, subscriber = spawn(fn -> receive do: (:stop -> :ok) end), gives a receive a `do:` whose content is a `->` clause, a body of its own, inside an fn body on the same line: violated by that sentence and by "two bodies do not share a line". The rule lists case, with and if, not receive, so this is a judgment that a receive is the same kind of construct; mix format accepts the line. No run has `if ..., do: ..., else: ...`, a `for`, or a function that mixes the two forms, and the capture sentence has nothing to apply to (the only capture, sonnet-2 line 168 &wait_for_stop/0, is a bare function reference). haiku-2 and sonnet-2 write every body as do ... end, including those holding an fn (haiku-2 lines 154-160, sonnet-2 lines 166-170): clean.

"Write pipelines that start with a value and read top to bottom" (changed): the sentence that would decide is "A pipeline never sits on one line, however short", together with the kind-or-mode sentence, but no file contains a |> operator, so the rule is not exercised in 4 of 4.

"Group tests by function and name them by behaviour", per test name. haiku-1 (15, all clean), including 81 "does nothing for a topic with no subscribers" (borderline clean, as every earlier sweep). haiku-2 (13, all clean): 49 "adds the subscriber to the topic and returns :ok" names the effect first, clean; 39 "fails to start without a :mailer option" clean. sonnet-1 (16, 2 violated): 37 "returns :ok for a pid" (body only line 38: assert Subscriptions.subscribe(server, "news", self()) == :ok) and 41 "returns :ok for an email address" (body only line 42), the same shape as 2026-10-23 haiku-1 line 34; 168 "keeps the server running" borderline clean as before. sonnet-2 (15, all clean), including 105 "does nothing for a topic without subscribers" and 130 "leaves the server running" (borderline clean). No describe block joins two functions: haiku-1 splits publish/3 into "publish/3 to pid subscribers" and "publish/3 to email subscribers" (function plus condition); haiku-2 adds "start_link/1"; sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 each add two exit conditions ("when a subscribed process exits" / "... exits normally", and "when a subscribed process has exited" with setup [:subscribe_other_process_and_email, :stop_other_process] / "when a subscribed process is killed").

"Wait for messages, not for time": haiku-1 waits for :DOWN with the caused reason (lines 125, 136, 148, 161: :normal, :boom, :normal, :normal) but then calls await_subscribers/4 (lines 181-195), a loop that polls subscribers/2 with Process.sleep(5) at line 192 up to 100 times; its comment at lines 179-180 says this covers the server's own :DOWN arriving late. The rule's "Do not use `Process.sleep/1` to wait for asynchronous work" decides: violated. The other three match the :DOWN reason (:normal or :killed), put a synchronous call or an assert_receive before refute_received (haiku-2 line 91, sonnet-2 line 100) or use refute_receive with its timeout (sonnet-1 lines 127-128, 135-136). sonnet-1 line 142 spawn(fn -> Process.sleep(:infinity) end) is a subscriber body, not counted, as before. The one-shot assert Process.alive?(server) lines (haiku-1 85, haiku-2 150, sonnet-1 169, sonnet-2 131) are assertions, not polling.

"Start processes with `start_supervised!/1`": haiku-2 is the only run testing a start failure, and line 43 is assert {:error, _reason} = start_supervised({Subscriptions, name: name}) inside capture_log: start_supervised/1 as the rule asks, but the reason is left open, so violated on "To assert that a start fails, call `start_supervised/1` and match the reason.", the same grading as 2026-10-23 haiku-1 line 166. No run calls start_link. Subscribers: sonnet-2 starts them with start_supervised!(Supervisor.child_spec({Task, &wait_for_stop/0}, id: make_ref(), restart: :temporary)); the others use bare spawn/1 or spawn_link/1 (sonnet-1 line 88), clean as before.

The other graded rules are clean in 4 of 4. All four use async: true with a setup_all Registry keyed by Module.concat(module, test) and a behaviour-implementing test mailer that finds the test pid through Process.info(self(), :registered_name); every server is start_supervised! under that name and setup returns a map matched in test heads; no Process.register, application env, :meck or redefinition of Notify.Mailer. Every == has the call on the left; no elem/2, no bind-then-==; sonnet-1 line 70 and sonnet-2 line 65 bind expected = [...] and compare the call to it whole, clean. Directive order: use then alias in haiku-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2; use, import ExUnit.CaptureLog, alias in haiku-2.

Changed rules outside this case's list, checked for other_violations: "Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call": no call takes a multi-line map, struct or keyword list, no literal has more than six elements, and no assertion's expected value is spread over lines. sonnet-2 lines 167-169, start_supervised!( / Supervisor.child_spec({Task, &wait_for_stop/0}, id: make_ref(), restart: :temporary) / ), has a nested call that mix format moved onto its own line; the rule's text names maps, structs and keyword lists, and nested calls are allowed elsewhere in the skill, so it is not counted, but the text does not settle this shape. The capture placeholder sentence: no capture uses &1 or &2. The `->` clause rule: every one-line clause is under 70 characters (sonnet-1 line 90 message -> send(test_pid, {:other_received, message}) is 52) and haiku-1's cond (lines 184-194) is broken as the rule asks. The elem/2 sentence: no elem/2. other_violations is empty in all four runs.

Tests were run from copies in the scratch folder with elixir -r test-writing-input.ex subscriptions_test.exs on Elixir 1.20.3 (OTP 29), 20 times each: every run passed every time with no warnings or log output (haiku-1 15 tests, haiku-2 13, sonnet-1 16, sonnet-2 15). All four pass mix format --check-formatted, confirming format_ok in result.json. Against 2026-10-23 (skill): haiku again breaks Start processes with an open start-failure reason (haiku-2 line 43 now, haiku-1 line 166 then), goes from violated to clean on Group tests, and from clean to violated on Wait for messages (haiku-1's sleep poll); both haiku runs now read processes.md (0 of 2 then). Sonnet again has :ok-only test names (sonnet-1 lines 37 and 41 now, sonnet-2 line 108 then) and has one `do:` violation (sonnet-1 line 175) on the newly graded rule.
